name: Japanese woodblock print
material: relief-printed woodblocks, ink/pigment and absorbent paper; Edo ukiyo-e commonly uses separate blocks for colors
fabrication_process: carver cuts relief key and color blocks
printer inks blocks and rubs paper with baren
edge_behavior: Edges are carved/printed: crisp graphic contour with occasional organic print variation, not anti-aliased vector perfection.
color_behavior: Flat color regions with limited layered overprinting and selective gradients; paper tone remains present.
surface_behavior: Mulberry-type paper absorbency and slight emboss/pressure cues; ink sits as a print, not glossy digital paint.
composition_behavior: Use bold cropping, diagonals, patterned negative space and page-aware composition; perspective may be stylized but internally coherent.
structural_limitations: each extra color implies another block/printing pass
fine gradients should look printed, not airbrushed
photographic bokeh is foreign unless deliberately hybridized
aging_weathering: fading, edge wear and paper discoloration depend on artifact state; do not force antique damage for a newly printed work

prompt_fragments.core: Rebuild the scene as a carved-and-printed image: authoritative keyline, flat color blocks, visible paper, precise registration with subtle hand-print variation, and selective bokashi rather than digital gradients.

evaluation_criteria: keyline reads as carved print line
color regions behave as block impressions
gradation looks like bokashi when used
composition feels designed for a sheet

sources.supports: designer/carver/printer/publisher workflow, cherry blocks, mulberry paper, separate color blocks

scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
